rules.title: Limit your resume to exactly one page
rules.why: Consulting recruiters screen resumes in under 10 seconds. Keeping your resume to exactly one page is a critical test of your ability to synthesize information and prioritize your impact.

source.note: The absolute maximum length for student consulting candidates is one page.

rules.title: Remove the photo — consulting resumes never include one
rules.why: In line with professional services standards in major markets, including a photo on a consulting resume is unnecessary and often leads to automatic rejection due to anti-bias screening protocols.

source.note: US and UK consulting firms mandate resumes without photos.

rules.title: Remove the photo — finance resumes never include one
rules.why: Finance and investment banking are highly conservative fields globally. Including a photo is considered unprofessional and is a common reason for immediate resume rejection, even in regions where photos are standard for other fields.

source.note: Finance resumes must not include photos.

rules.title: Limit your resume to exactly one page
rules.why: A strict one-page limit is universal in finance and investment banking recruiting for students and new graduates. Exceeding this limit is viewed as a failure of prioritization.

source.note: Finance/IB standard template requires exactly one page.

rules.title: Keep it under two pages
rules.why: Standard German CVs (Lebenslauf) should not exceed two pages for early-career candidates to remain concise and readable.

source.note: Germany section — standard early career CV length is up to 2 pages

rules.title: Use British English spelling for English CVs in Germany
rules.why: English-language CVs in Germany and Europe typically follow British English spelling conventions (e.g., "optimise", "colour").

source.note: English CVs in Europe typically follow British English spelling conventions

rules.title: Remove the declaration line
rules.why: Declaration lines are a regional South Asian convention; in Germany they are not used and waste valuable space.

source.note: declaration lines are not used in German CVs

rules.title: Keep it under two pages
rules.why: Indian resumes run longer than US ones, but campus recruiters and off-campus portals still skim; past two pages you're hiding your best work.

source.note: India commonly 2 pages for freshers

rules.title: Use one English spelling variant consistently
rules.why: Indian résumés are written in both British and American English — either is fine. Mixing en-US and en-GB spellings in the same document is what reads as careless.

source.note: consistency within one spelling convention; India accepts either

rules.title: Remove the photo — UK CVs never include one
rules.why: UK employers exclude CVs with photos to prevent discrimination bias under the Equality Act; a photo can lead to rejection before review.

source.note: UK section — photos discouraged due to discrimination legislation

rules.title: Remove date of birth / marital status / nationality
rules.why: Protected personal characteristics (age, marital status, nationality) are omitted from UK CVs to prevent bias and ensure compliance with UK anti-discrimination laws.

source.note: Avoid including personal information like age, date of birth, marital status, or nationality.

rules.title: Keep it under two pages
rules.why: UK early-career CVs are expected to be at most two pages long; going over two pages dilutes your key details and violates standard recruiters' expectations.

source.note: UK standard CV length for early career is up to 2 pages.

rules.title: Use British English spelling consistently
rules.why: UK applications must use British English spelling (e.g., "optimise", "colour") to show localization and consistency.

source.note: match spelling conventions to the target country (en-GB for the UK)

rules.title: Remove the declaration line
rules.why: Declaration lines are a regional South Asian convention; in the UK they are not used and waste valuable space.

source.note: declaration lines are not used in UK CVs

rules.title: Remove the photo — US resumes never include one
rules.why: US employers routinely discard resumes with photos to avoid discrimination-liability; a photo hurts you even when it's good.

source.note: US section — photos discouraged for bias/legal reasons

suggestion.after: No photo; use the space for a project or skills line

rules.title: Remove date of birth / marital status / nationality
rules.why: Protected personal information is never disclosed on US resumes; recruiters are trained to treat it as a red flag.

source.note: US candidates do not disclose protected personal information

rules.title: Cut to one page for early-career US applications
rules.why: US recruiters expect new-grad/intern resumes on a single page; extra pages dilute your strongest material in the 6-second skim.

source.note: US resumes 1–2 pages; 1 page standard for early career

rules.title: Use American English spelling throughout
rules.why: Mixed or British spellings (optimise, colour) read as unlocalized to US reviewers and keyword searches use American variants.

source.note: match spelling conventions to the target country

rules.title: Remove the declaration line
rules.why: "I hereby declare the above is true..." is an Indian/South-Asian convention; on a US resume it reads as boilerplate and wastes a line.

source.note: declaration lines are a regional convention, not used in US resumes

rules.title: Quantify a higher percentage of your experience and project bullets
rules.why: Consulting firms (McKinsey, BCG, Bain) heavily filter on quantified impact. Resumes with at least 70% of bullets containing numbers have a significantly higher callback rate.

source.note: Recruiter screens look for quantified achievements in every single project or job.

rules.title: Highlight leadership roles or awards on your resume
rules.why: MBB screeners look for evidence of leadership, initiative, and drive. This check looks for awards or explicit leadership keywords (e.g. Lead, Founder, President) in your positions/projects. If you have leadership experience not flagged by these keywords, ensure they are prominently described.

source.note: Leadership evidence is one of the three primary dimensions evaluated on MBB resumes.

rules.title: Add SQL to your skills — it is the primary data analyst tool
rules.why: SQL is the industry-standard database query language; almost all data analyst positions list it as a core requirement.

source.note: SQL is the most requested skill in data analyst job listings

rules.title: Include data visualization tools (Tableau, Power BI)
rules.why: Data analysts must translate raw data into actionable dashboards and visualizations; listing Tableau, Power BI, Looker, or Qlik demonstrates this capability.

source.note: Data visualization tool proficiency is a standard requirement for analyst positions

rules.title: Mention SystemVerilog, UVM, or key VLSI tools and design/verification concepts

params.label: SystemVerilog, UVM, HDLs, or VLSI toolchains

rules.why: Design Verification and VLSI engineers must list specific digital design/verification toolchains, hardware description languages (SystemVerilog, Verilog, VHDL), verification methodologies (UVM), or simulation tools.

source.note: Hardware/VLSI engineers must list specific EDA tools, protocols, and HDLs.

rules.title: Mention verification methodologies or testbench design (e.g. UVM, SystemVerilog TB)
rules.why: Verification engineers must demonstrate familiarity with structured verification methodologies (like UVM), writing testbenches, assertions (SVA), or coverage metrics.

source.note: Verification-focused roles look for exposure to simulation, coverage, and testbench structures.

rules.title: Specify logic synthesis or EDA simulation tools (e.g., Design Compiler, Xcelium, Vivado)
rules.why: Silicon development roles require familiarity with industry-standard EDA tools for design simulation, power profiling (Joules), synthesis (Design Compiler), or FPGA implementation (Vivado).

source.note: Demonstrating competence in Cadence, Synopsys, or Xilinx toolsuites is standard for VLSI hardware engineers.

rules.title: Add a Projects section to showcase hardware design or verification experience
rules.why: Hands-on hardware or software projects (e.g. custom accelerators, verification testbenches, FPGA beamformers) are essential proof of engineering competence.

source.note: Projects are a mandatory section to showcase hardware design and problem-solving capability.

rules.title: Emphasize previous silicon internships, co-ops, or design verification work experience
rules.why: Relevant internships, co-ops, or professional verification roles are highly valued in the semiconductor industry. Ensure you have a work experience section.

source.note: Practical engineering experience is the most heavily weighted component of the resume.

rules.title: Mention PCB design, HDL, or electrical laboratory skills

params.label: PCB design, HDL, or lab tools

rules.why: Electrical engineering candidates must demonstrate tool proficiency in PCB design (Altium, KiCad), HDLs (Verilog, VHDL), circuit simulation (SPICE), or laboratory test equipment (oscilloscopes).

source.note: Electrical engineers must list specific lab equipment and software toolchains.

rules.title: List FE Exam or EIT status (US engineering roles)
rules.why: Passing the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) exam is highly valued for US electrical engineering candidates aiming for power systems, MEP, or utility engineering careers.

source.note: FE/EIT status is standard professional registration preparation for US engineering positions.

rules.title: Add a Projects section to showcase engineering design experience
rules.why: Hands-on hardware or software projects (e.g. PCB layouts, microcontrollers, tapeouts) are critical proof of engineering competence for students.

source.note: Projects are a mandatory section to showcase engineering and problem-solving capability.

rules.title: Emphasize previous co-ops, internships, or engineering work experience
rules.why: Relevant co-ops, internships, or technical work experience are highly valued by electrical engineering recruiters. Ensure you have a work experience section.

source.note: Practical engineering experience is the most heavily weighted component of the resume.

rules.title: Add your GPA (essential for finance recruiting screens)
rules.why: Finance recruiters use academic GPA as a primary filtering metric for internships and new-grad entry roles. Omitting it completely is a red flag.

source.note: GPA is a mandatory field for entry-level financial analyst resumes

rules.title: Highlight Advanced Excel or Financial Modeling skills
rules.why: Practical finance relies on spreadsheets and models; you must explicitly list Excel, financial modeling, valuation, or DCF in your skills to pass screening keyword checks.

source.note: Excel and modeling are core technical requirements

rules.title: Mention relevant finance certifications (e.g., CFA, Bloomberg)
rules.why: Finance certifications like CFA Level I or Bloomberg Terminal certifications show industry knowledge and self-directed preparation.

source.note: Certifications showcase dedication and baseline technical skills

rules.title: Quantify a higher percentage of your experience and project bullets
rules.why: Investment banking recruiters expect a very high density of numbers in resume bullets (specifically transaction sizes in dollars, growth rates, and margins). At least 70% of your highlights should contain numbers.

source.note: IB bullets must be highly quantified with transaction values and metrics.

rules.title: Highlight Excel and financial modeling skills
rules.why: Excel and financial modeling (DCF, LBO, M&A) are core technical competencies for investment banking analyst recruits. Listing them explicitly is necessary to pass screens.

source.note: Advanced Excel and modeling proficiency is a baseline requirement.

rules.title: Mention relevant finance certifications (e.g., CFA, Bloomberg)
rules.why: Finance-specific certifications like the CFA Level I candidate status or Bloomberg Market Concepts (BMC) show commitment to financial markets and enhance early-career credibility.

source.note: Financial certifications validate analytical skills and industry interest.

rules.title: Quantify your business impact using %, $, or scale metrics
rules.why: MBA admissions committees look for quantified results (revenue, costs, percentages, team size) to gauge the scale and significance of your achievements, rather than a list of tasks.

source.note: Stacy Blackman recommends quantifying every accomplishment with percentages, numbers, or dollars.

rules.title: Demonstrate explicit leadership scope or management evidence
rules.why: Leadership potential is the single most important dimension evaluated by MBA admissions screeners. Your resume must contain explicit evidence of leadership, initiative, team coordination, or project stewardship.

source.note: Top-tier MBA programs filter candidates heavily on proven leadership experience and scope.

rules.title: Highlight career progression and promotions
rules.why: MBA admissions look for candidates with a trajectory of career growth and increasing responsibility. This check highlights if there is no clear evidence of title progression or promotions.

source.note: Showcase promotions or logical progression of titles to prove your trajectory of growth.

rules.title: Show extracurricular involvement and community impact
rules.why: MBA programs value candidates who contribute outside their professional jobs. Extracurricular activities, volunteer work, or club leadership demonstrate well-roundedness and community initiative.

source.note: Active extracurricular and community involvement is highly weighted by admissions boards.

rules.title: Mention CAD, FEA, or mechanical engineering design tools
rules.why: Mechanical engineering internships expect familiarity with standard design and simulation tools. Listing CAD/FEA software is critical to pass core technical screens.

source.note: Mechanical engineering resumes must list core software tools like CAD/FEA.

rules.title: List FE Exam or EIT status (US engineering roles)
rules.why: Passing the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) exam to earn EIT status is a standard professional milestone for mechanical engineers in the US, showing intent to pursue PE licensing.

source.note: FE exam or EIT certification is highly valued for US entry-level engineering roles.

rules.title: Add a Projects section to showcase engineering design experience
rules.why: Engineering candidates must show hand-on design, analysis, and fabrication experience. A structured projects section is a mandatory component.

source.note: Academic or personal engineering projects are essential to demonstrate hands-on competence.

rules.title: Emphasize previous co-ops, internships, or engineering work experience
rules.why: Co-op and internship experiences are the single most heavily weighted factor in hiring new graduates. Ensure you have a work experience section listing your engineering experience.

source.note: Work experience in engineering, co-ops, or internships is preferred above all else.

rules.title: Quantify your product outcomes using user and business metrics
rules.why: Product Managers are evaluated on their ability to drive business and user outcomes (e.g. conversion rates, retention, DAU/MAU, user growth) rather than just listing shipped features or tasks.

source.note: Exponent highlights that PM resumes must treat accomplishments as products and measure outcomes using user/business metrics rather than listing responsibilities.

rules.title: Demonstrate user research, interviews, or experimentation
rules.why: Strong product managers ground their decisions in customer insight and data. Evidence of user interviews, usability testing, A/B testing, or data experiments proves user empathy and structured product discovery.

source.note: Lenny's Newsletter emphasizes that demonstrating customer empathy and data-informed decision-making (e.g. A/B testing, user research) is key to standing out as a PM.

rules.title: Showcase cross-functional collaboration and stakeholder alignment
rules.why: Product management is inherently collaborative and requires leading without authority. Describing collaboration across engineering, design, marketing, or business teams is critical.

source.note: PMs operate at the intersection of business, design, and engineering, and must show clear evidence of driving cross-functional alignment.

rules.title: Add a Projects section — it carries a student SWE resume
rules.why: With little work history, projects are the main evidence of engineering ability; recruiter-side tools (e.g. HackerRank's hiring-agent) score personal projects and open-source work directly.

source.note: recruiter-side evaluator scores projects/OSS as primary dimensions

rules.title: Add your GitHub profile link
rules.why: SWE recruiters and automated evaluators look for a GitHub link to verify project claims; its absence removes your cheapest credibility signal.

source.note: GitHub enrichment is a core stage of recruiter-side evaluation

rules.title: Link each project to its code or demo
rules.why: An unlinked project claim can't be verified; a link turns an assertion into evidence.

source.note: project verification requires repository links

rules.title: Consider adding your GPA (if 3.0+/4.0 or equivalent)
rules.why: Early-career screeners often filter on GPA; omitting it when it's decent makes you look like you're hiding it. Skip only if it's genuinely low.

source.note: education-level and GPA checks are standard early-career screens

rules.title: List relevant coursework under education
rules.why: For students, coursework is searchable keyword surface and evidence of exposure recruiters can't get from an empty work history.

source.note: early-career resumes lean on education detail

rules.title: Quantify your bullet points
rules.why: Bullets without numbers state duties, not outcomes. "Reduced p95 latency 40%" survives the 6-second skim; "worked on backend" does not.

source.note: human skim, not ATS auto-rejection, is what kills weak bullets

rules.title: Link each certification to its verification URL
rules.why: Unlinked certifications are harder for recruiters to verify. Adding a verification link (e.g. from Google, Microsoft, Coursera, Udemy, Bloomberg, or Credly) provides immediate proof of your credential.

source.note: List the name of the certification, the authority, date, and a link to verify it.
